text: Soon they saw a woman hobbling along the path, and Brown recognized Goody Cloyse, a pious old lady who had taught him his catechism in youth and was still his spiritual adviser. <break time="0.8s" /> Ashamed to be seen with such a companion, Brown hid among the trees, while the traveler went forward and touched her withered neck with what seemed the serpents tail. <break time="0.8s" /> The devil, screamed the old lady, but instead of running away, she greeted him warmly as an old friend and complained that someone had stolen her broomstick. <break time="0.8s" /> She added that she was going to the meeting that night, where, it was said, a nice young man was to be taken into communion. <break time="0.8s" /> The traveler threw down his staff at her feet, and the old woman vanished in an instant, leaving Brown astonished that his own teacher was going to such a meeting. <break time="0.8s" /> As they walked on, the traveler made a new staff from a maple branch, and its twigs withered and dried up the moment his fingers touched them. <break time="0.8s" /> Not another step will I budge on this errand, said Brown stubbornly, sitting down on a stump, for why should I leave my dear Faith because an old woman goes to the devil. <break time="0.8s" /> Saying that Brown would think better of it by and by, the traveler threw him the maple staff and was out of sight as if he had vanished into the deepening gloom.
